question: What is the content-hash cache hit rate on real browsing?
why_wall_clock_bound: The number that matters is the CROSS-DAY rate, which is a property of how sites version and re-serve their bundles across deploys. It cannot be synthesised from a scripted burst and cannot be produced on demand at the end of the phase. That is why the recorder ships in wave 1 and is merely READ in plan 00-04.

recorder.note: The one instance in this phase that is deliberately NOT disposable. Guest-enabled and therefore bound to 127.0.0.1 only, permanently.

rates.cross_day_undefined_reason: No content hash has been observed on two or more distinct calendar days yet, so the cross-day rate is UNDEFINED — not zero. Zero would assert that caching measurably never works.

collection.live_mode_available: The operator may additionally point their real browser at 127.0.0.1:8998 for a normal work session. Higher realism, lower reproducibility. Entirely their choice; the scripted sessions run unattended regardless.

provisional_note: CLOSED OUT by plan 00-04. results/SPIKE-10.json is now the authority and go-no-go.json is the only artifact later phases may import; this file is the collection log that produced them and is kept for provenance, not as a threshold source. Collection has STOPPED: the twice-daily LaunchAgent was uninstalled and the recorder instance on 8998 was killed, both deliberately, so that no background job is left running on the operator's machine. The cross-day rate is therefore still UNDEFINED and will stay that way until someone re-installs the agent with `bash scripts/spike/recorder-agent.sh install` and lets it span at least two calendar days. The database is preserved at the path above.
privacy: cache_log stores only {ts, url, sha256, bytes, content_type, status}. No bodies, no headers, no cookies, no auth material. .spike/ is gitignored, so neither the database nor any recorded URL enters git.
